title: Mock 7 · Tough II: Exam Simulation
blurb: Final-boss set with close distractors: HWM fees, interaction effect, TWRR from portfolio values, combined tax computation and 2026 updates.

questions.q: Which statement about investment risks is NOT correct?
options: Depreciation of the investor's home currency reduces returns on foreign assets
Treasury bills have practically no liquidity risk
Risk is mathematically represented by standard deviation around the expected return
Regulatory risk can be mitigated by diversifying across industries and geographies
questions.explanation: Depreciation in the home currency INCREASES returns on foreign assets; appreciation reduces them. The other statements match the workbook.
hints: Correct: this is the false statement.

questions.q: According to the workbook, the real risk-free rate is determined by the interaction between:
options: Subjective desire for current consumption and objective factors like investment opportunities and the economy's real growth rate
SEBI policy and stock market valuations
The coupon on G-Secs and the repo rate only
questions.explanation: The real risk-free rate is set by subjective factors (desire for consumption) and objective factors (available investment opportunities and real growth of the economy).
hints: Wrong: these are added on top of the real rate.
Wrong: not how the workbook describes it.

questions.q: Which statement about depositories and DPs is NOT correct?
options: NSDL and CDSL are the two SEBI-registered depositories
DPs are appointed by the depository with the approval of SEBI
The depository maintains investor-level accounts while the DP maintains company-level accounts
Stock brokers and scheduled commercial banks can be registered as DPs
questions.explanation: It is the reverse: investor-level accounts are held and maintained by the DP, and company-level accounts by the depository.

questions.q: A listed company issues shares only to Qualified Institutional Buyers such as mutual funds, banks and financial institutions. This is a:
questions.explanation: QIP is a private placement of shares by a listed company to Qualified Institutional Buyers, under SEBI's eligibility, quantum and pricing norms.
hints: Wrong: rights go to existing shareholders.
Wrong: OFS is a sale by existing holders.
Wrong: FPO is open to the public.

questions.q: Stock A: P/E 40, EPS growth 40%. Stock B: P/E 20, EPS growth 10%. Using PEG, which conclusion is correct?
options: B is cheaper because its P/E is lower
A (PEG 1.0) looks fairly valued and B (PEG 2.0) looks overvalued
A is overvalued because its P/E is higher
questions.explanation: PEG A = 40/40 = 1.0 (fair), PEG B = 20/10 = 2.0 (greater than 1 suggests overvalued). PEG adjusts P/E for growth.
hints: Wrong: a high P/E can be justified by growth.

questions.q: The key limitation of asset-based (replacement value) valuation is that it:
options: Cannot be used for financial institutions
Does not recognise the value of future profits, cash flows and innovation
questions.explanation: Asset-based valuation does not recognise future profits and cash flows or future value creation through research and innovation.
hints: Wrong: it is used for financial institutions.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an assumption of technical analysis as listed in the workbook?
options: Prices move in trends that persist for appreciable lengths of time
Market price is determined by supply and demand
Shifts in supply and demand can be detected in the action of the market itself
questions.explanation: Technical analysis assumes price adjustments are NOT instantaneous and prices move in trends.

questions.q: A bond with a 9% coupon is trading at a premium to its face value. Which is most likely true?
options: Its YTM is below 9% because market rates are below the coupon
It must be a zero coupon bond
questions.explanation: A bond sells at a premium when the market interest rate is below the coupon; then YTM < coupon rate.
hints: Wrong: that is a discount bond.
Wrong: that is a par bond.

questions.q: Statement I: For short-term instruments, the modifier '+' can be used with A1 to A4. Statement II: For long-term instruments, modifiers '+' and '-' can be used with categories AAA to D. Which is correct?
questions.explanation: Short-term: '+' modifier for A1 to A4 (true). Long-term: modifiers apply to AA through C only, not AAA or D (II false).

questions.q: Derivatives are described as a zero-sum game. This conclusion assumes:
options: There are no taxes and no transaction costs
questions.explanation: Net positions of buyer and seller sum to zero under the usual assumptions of no taxes and no transaction costs.
hints: Wrong: applies to exchange contracts too.

questions.q: In the REIT structure, the entity that independently values real estate assets for fair pricing is the:
questions.explanation: The REIT structure includes a Valuer that independently values real estate assets.
hints: Wrong: ensures compliance and oversees the manager.

questions.q: According to the workbook, which factor fund type tends to provide resilience and perform well in bear markets?
questions.explanation: Quality factor funds (low debt, stable earnings growth) perform well in bear markets. Momentum is effective in bull markets; value does well in recovery and bull phases.
hints: Wrong: does well in recovery and bull markets.

questions.q: A PMS client asks the portfolio manager to buy shares intraday and square off the same day with no delivery, purely to profit from price swings. Under the regulations, the PM:
options: Shall not enter into such speculative transactions settled otherwise than by actual delivery
May do so if the client signs a waiver
May do so up to 25% of AUM
May do so only for accredited investors
questions.explanation: The PM shall not indulge in speculative transactions, i.e., any purchase or sale settled otherwise than by actual delivery or transfer, except transactions in derivatives.

questions.q: Which requirement does NOT apply to a co-investment portfolio manager, as noted in the workbook?
options: Minimum investment amount per client of ₹50 lakh
questions.explanation: The ₹50 lakh minimum does not apply to co-investment PMs (they are also exempt from maintaining net worth and appointing a custodian). Other obligations continue.

questions.q: Which of the following records is NOT specifically listed among the books a portfolio manager must maintain?
options: Copy of the balance sheet for each accounting period
Records supporting every investment decision with data, facts and opinion
Personal income tax returns of each client's family members
questions.explanation: PMs maintain balance sheet, P&L, auditor's report, statement of financial position and records supporting every investment transaction or recommendation. Clients' family tax returns are not required.

questions.q: A PMS with a 20% performance fee under a High Water Mark starts at ₹1 crore; values at year ends are ₹1.25 crore, ₹1.10 crore and ₹1.40 crore (ignore other fees and assume no fee reduces the base). The performance fee in Year 3 is:
questions.explanation: HWM after Year 1 = ₹1.25 crore. Year 3 fee applies only on gains above ₹1.25 crore: (1.40 - 1.25) = ₹15 lakh x 20% = ₹3,00,000.
hints: Wrong: charges on gain over original ₹1 crore.
Wrong: charges on Year 3 gain from ₹1.10 crore.
Wrong: value exceeds the HWM, so a fee is due.

questions.q: Which detail must be included in the periodic report a PM furnishes to its client?
options: Commission paid to distributor(s) for that particular client
Names of other clients of the PM
questions.explanation: The periodic report includes portfolio composition and value, transactions, beneficial interest, expenses, risks, defaults/downgrades and details of commission paid to distributors for the particular client.

questions.q: Under the SMART ODR mechanism, an investor's dispute request is assigned to a Market Infrastructure Institution's ODR platform:
options: By the investor's choice of arbitrator
Through the portfolio manager's compliance officer
questions.explanation: Investors may approach any MII through the SMART ODR portal; requests are auto-assigned to an MII ODR platform on a round-robin basis.
hints: Wrong: APMI has no role here.

questions.q: In the agreement of a discretionary portfolio manager, which condition about client liability must be included?
options: The client's liability shall not exceed his investment with the portfolio manager
The client is liable for the PM's operational losses
The client's liability is capped at the performance fee
questions.explanation: In the case of a discretionary PM, the agreement contains a condition that the liability of a client shall not exceed his investment with the PM.

questions.q: Statement I: SAA rebalances less frequently, e.g., annually, to restore target weights. Statement II: TAA is ideal for passive long-term investors seeking steady growth. Which is correct?
questions.explanation: SAA rebalances less frequently to restore targets. TAA suits experienced investors or professional managers with market expertise; SAA suits passive long-term investors.

questions.q: For low-priority goals such as buying a farm house or a luxury car, the workbook says investment approaches are usually:
options: Matched to goal dates with fixed deposits
questions.explanation: For low-priority goals, whose non-achievement is not particularly painful, more aggressive investment approaches are usually taken.
hints: Wrong: that suits near-term high-priority goals.
Wrong: that suits near-term high-priority goals.

questions.q: Keeping some liquidity so the portfolio can take advantage of market opportunities as asset classes become over- or under-valued falls under which liquidity need category?
questions.explanation: The workbook lists liquidity needs as emergency cash, near-term goals and investment flexibility; the ability to exploit opportunities is investment flexibility.
hints: Wrong: near-term goals are known goals within a year.

questions.q: Which is a MACROECONOMIC factor rather than a style factor in factor-based investing?
questions.explanation: Macroeconomic factors include inflation, economic growth, interest rates and liquidity conditions; value, momentum, size, quality and low volatility are style factors.

questions.q: Portfolio vs benchmark: Tech Wp 45%, Rp 15%, Wb 30%, Rb 11%; FMCG Wp 25%, Rp 7%, Wb 40%, Rb 8%; Banks Wp 30%, Rp 9%, Wb 30%, Rb 10%. The interaction effect is:
hints: Wrong: this is the allocation effect.
Wrong: this is the selection effect.
Wrong: this is the total excess return.

questions.q: A portfolio starts at ₹10 lakh and grows to ₹11 lakh at the end of Year 1, when the client adds ₹4 lakh. At the end of Year 2 it is worth ₹16.5 lakh. The annualised TWRR is:
hints: Wrong: this is the 2-year cumulative TWRR.

questions.q: A poorly diversified portfolio ranks higher on the Treynor ratio than on the Sharpe ratio compared with its peers. The most likely reason is that:
options: The risk-free rate differs between the two ratios
Treynor ignores unsystematic risk, which is high in a poorly diversified portfolio
questions.explanation: Treynor uses beta (systematic risk) and ignores unsystematic risk; any ranking difference is due to diversification levels. For fully diversified portfolios rankings are identical.
hints: Wrong: the same Rf is used.
Wrong: Sharpe is based on SD.

questions.q: In a financial year, a resident PMS investor realises STCG of ₹4 lakh and LTCG of ₹2 lakh on listed equity (no other gains). Ignoring surcharge and cess, total capital gains tax is:
hints: Wrong: ignores the ₹1.25 lakh LTCG exemption.

questions.q: Which statement about NRIs investing through PMS is correct as per the workbook?
options: PIS approval from RBI is mandatory for every PMS investment
NRIs may do intraday trading and short selling through PMS
NRIs may use NRE funds for F&O trading through PMS
PIS approval is not required for PMS investments, and NRIs cannot engage in intraday trading or short selling
questions.explanation: PIS approval is not required for PMS since the PM takes decisions; NRIs cannot engage in intraday trading or short selling; F&O is only through NRO funds.

questions.q: Under the PaRRVA framework, from which date are only PaRRVA-verified risk and return metrics permitted for client communication?
questions.explanation: Intermediaries get a 2-year transition to use pre-PaRRVA historical data; effective May 03, 2028 only PaRRVA-verified metrics are allowed.
hints: Wrong: date of the SEBI circular.
Wrong: date from which the 2026 workbook applies to exams.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the five cyber resiliency goals of SEBI's CSCRF?
questions.explanation: The five goals are Anticipate, Withstand, Contain, Recover and Evolve.
